coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 only (135–145 bpm ceiling). You ran hard yesterday (12 miles at 132 avg), and you're 36 days out—this is taper discipline, not fitness building. Your recovery score is 57/100 and sleep was gutted at 5.19h last night; a submax day protects your central nervous system and allows adaptation from the work you've already done. Keep it flat or rolling, focus on form and breathing, and call it done by mid-morning so you're not adding cortisol stress before Friday's shakeout.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Prioritize carbs and protein at every meal today—you're in taper and need glycogen for Saturday's long run, plus your short sleep means elevated recovery demand. Aim for 1.2–1.6g carb per kg bodyweight across the day, split evenly; post-run (within 30 min), take 30–40g carbs + 15–20g protein. Because you travel constantly, rely on packable carbs (oats, rice cakes, dates, energy bars) and a protein source you control (powder, jerky, canned fish). Hydration: at least 3L water today, more if you're in a dry climate.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your sleep debt is real—5.19h is not a blip, it's a hole. Tonight, non-negotiable: no screens after 21:00, dark room (blackout curtains), aim for 8+ hours. Your resting HR is trending down (62 vs 65.2 avg), which is good, but short sleep will undo that. Consider a 20–minute nap if your schedule allows post-run. Foam roll lower legs and hips for 10 minutes; you've got vert-heavy terrain coming and dense tissue work pays dividends in taper.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the psychological grind of taper—your body is fresh but your mind feels like you're doing nothing. That feeling is the point. Trust the process: you ran 47 miles last week and built the engine; this week is about showing up rested and sharp for race week. Use today's easy run to visualize Kranjska Gora's alpine sections—technical descents, exposed ridge running, sparse aid. Mental rehearsal counts as training. Stay present; don't let work stress bleed into your taper.
